aboutGame.title: What is Windgate?
paragraphs: Windgate is an open-world multiplayer sandbox on Roblox from developer Defaultio, where players chop trees, haul logs, mine ore, and sell what they gather to fund the next upgrade. The name is best known in Lumber Tycoon 2, where Windgate is a named landmark that players travel to rather than a step in the standard lumber loop.

Progress comes from tool tiers, carry capacity, and route knowledge. A stronger axe unlocks denser and rarer wood, storage and vehicles cut the travel time between patches, and processed goods such as refined iron or lavawood sell for far more than raw logs. The Windgate Wiki gathers that knowledge into step-by-step guides, tier tables, and build walkthroughs.

explore.title: Explore Windgate Wiki
explore.description: Eight Windgate Wiki modules cover the full game loop: beginner routes, money making, tools and equipment, wood tiers, building, multiplayer, and updates.

modules.name: Windgate Wiki Beginner Guide
modules.description: A step-by-step start for new players: what to bring, how to plan a first route, and the habits that keep early sessions profitable.

highlights.detail: Stock up first: repair or replace your axe and keep a cash reserve before you travel.
Start from a landmark you already know so you can measure how far you have gone.
Track two or three distinctive features on the way out so you can find your way back.
Run a fixed loop: mid-tier hardwood first for a guaranteed baseline, then rare spawns in order.
Fill the remaining capacity with the highest tier wood your axe can actually fell.
Sell or mill the load, then bank 20-30% of the payout before buying upgrades.

modules.name: Windgate Wiki Gameplay Guide
modules.description: How the core loop fits together: chopping, hauling, selling, and the landmarks that decide what a trip is worth.

highlights.label: Explore
highlights.detail: Windgate is an optional landmark, so treat it as an exploration objective rather than a step in the lumber loop.

highlights.label: Routes
highlights.detail: Confirm the current route before you commit, because landmarks shift between game versions.

highlights.label: Selling
highlights.detail: Sell or mill high-value loads instead of dumping raw logs at the base price.

highlights.label: Storage
highlights.detail: Storage near your sell point and furnace removes the travel time that eats into every run.

highlights.label: Upgrades
highlights.detail: Spend first on a stronger axe and more carry capacity, since they raise income on every trip.

highlights.label: Patience
highlights.detail: Plan for two or three attempts and compare notes with other players once you are done.

modules.name: Windgate Wiki Tips and Tricks
modules.description: Small decisions that protect your time: load management, route planning, banking habits, and the mistakes that drain profit.

highlights.label: Load
highlights.detail: Empty your inventory completely before a run, because dead weight costs a full trip's profit.

highlights.label: Route
highlights.detail: Follow a fixed loop every session so muscle memory replaces decision time.

highlights.label: Bank
highlights.detail: Keep a 20-30% cash buffer so a single bad run cannot wipe your progress.

highlights.label: Spawns
highlights.detail: Farm a nearby mid-tier patch while you wait for a rare spawn window to open.

highlights.label: Backup
highlights.detail: Carry a backup axe so a repair or a swap never ends the session early.

highlights.label: Group
highlights.detail: Team up for timed event wood, since solo hunting misses spawns and burns players out.

modules.name: Windgate Wiki Tools and Equipment
modules.description: Axes, vehicles, storage, and processing gear compared, with the upgrade order that pays for itself fastest.

highlights.label: Starter Axe
highlights.detail: Fells common wood slowly, which is enough to learn routes and build a first cash buffer.

highlights.label: Improved Axe
highlights.detail: Cuts uncommon hardwoods and some rares, and is the first upgrade that visibly raises income.

highlights.label: High-Tier Axe
highlights.detail: Fells rare trees such as ebony, and is the entry requirement for real rare-wood farming.

highlights.label: Endgame Axe
highlights.detail: Handles every wood tier at the fastest swing speed for maximum logs per trip.

modules.name: Windgate Wiki Game Modes and Worlds
modules.description: What changes as you move from early sessions to mid-game setups and the Windgate push itself.

highlights.label: Early Game
highlights.detail: Learn the map, find your sell point and storage, and earn steadily before chasing rares.

highlights.label: Mid Game
highlights.detail: Tool upgrades and storage become the bottleneck, and running out of inventory space blocks progress.

highlights.label: Pre-Push
highlights.detail: Stockpile roughly 1.5-2x your estimated need and scout the approach with an empty inventory.

highlights.label: Post-Gate
highlights.detail: Rebuild your economy on the new tool tier, because pre-gate income no longer matches the costs.

modules.name: Windgate Wiki Tier List
modules.description: Wood and tree tiers ranked by payout, spawn rarity, and how much cargo capacity each one really costs.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: Lavawood and other refined or limited-spawn woods: the highest ceiling, for planned sessions only.

highlights.label: A
highlights.detail: Rare trees such as ebony, worth a long deep-grove route once you own a high-tier axe.

highlights.label: B
highlights.detail: Mid-tier hardwoods, the steady daily earner and the baseline of every money loop.

highlights.label: C
highlights.detail: Starter softwoods: reliable but low value, so use them only until your first upgrade.

modules.name: Windgate Wiki Multiplayer Guide
modules.description: Playing with others: finding a real community server, splitting roles on a run, and trading without getting burned.

highlights.label: Servers
highlights.detail: Verify an invite before joining, and treat unsolicited DMs and comment spam as red flags.

highlights.label: Roles
highlights.detail: Split chopping, hauling, and selling so one group run beats four solo runs.

highlights.label: Trades
highlights.detail: Check availability, trade history, and timing before paying a premium for a rare tool.

highlights.label: Events
highlights.detail: Coordinate timed spawns in chat, because one message can save a twenty-minute search.

modules.name: Windgate Wiki Updates and Patch Notes
modules.description: How to keep your routes current with patch notes, community wikis, and checks inside your own server.

highlights.label: Patch Notes
highlights.detail: Read the official notes first, since they are authoritative even when they are terse.

highlights.label: Community Wiki
highlights.detail: Structured and cross-referenced, but it can lag behind a fresh update.

highlights.label: Discord
highlights.detail: The fastest firsthand reports, with quality that varies, so cross-check anything important.

highlights.label: In-Game Check
highlights.detail: Old routes go stale, so confirm landmarks and prompts in your own server.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about Windgate, its core loop, and how to use the Windgate Wiki.

items.question: What is Windgate Wiki?
items.answer: Windgate Wiki is a fan-built guide hub for Windgate, the open-world sandbox in Lumber Tycoon 2 from developer Defaultio. It collects beginner routes, money-making methods, wood tier tables, tool upgrades, and building walkthroughs in one place.

items.question: What should I bring on my first Windgate run?
items.answer: A working axe, a cash reserve for tools and repairs, and basic map knowledge. A friend helps you recover from wrong turns faster, and a daytime session makes navigation far easier.

items.question: Why do different Windgate guides disagree?
items.answer: Windgate sits inside a game that receives periodic updates, and much of what is known about it comes from player experience rather than official documentation. When two guides conflict, trust the more recent one and confirm the details in your own server.

items.question: Is Windgate required for progression?
items.answer: No. Windgate works as an optional exploration objective rather than a mandatory milestone, so you can chop, build, and sell for a long time before you ever visit it.

items.question: Which trees are worth farming first in Windgate?
items.answer: Mid-tier hardwoods are the steady earner. Build your income on them before chasing rare trees such as ebony, and only run limited-spawn or event woods once your gear is upgraded.

items.question: Does Windgate Wiki list working codes?
items.answer: No. The wiki focuses on guides, tier tables, and mechanics, and it does not publish redeem codes for Windgate.
